title: Slate
description: The complete set of matches a collection run operates on, known before collection begins. Collectors receive the slate whole and choose their own fan-out — an odds collector iterates matches, a social collector reads the teams and polls per team, a table collector works per league. The rule that selected these matches is recorded alongside them, because a slate collected under one rule is not interchangeable with a slate collected under another.

slate_id.description: Content hash over the canonical match set, in the same `sha256:<hex>` form as snapshot_hash. Content-addressed so that two runs over the same matches are recognisably the same slate. A run record may additionally carry its own run identifier; the two answer different questions.

selection.description: How these matches were chosen. Recorded so a slate stays interpretable after the rule changes.

matches.description: Match references. Deliberately thin: identity, timing, and the entities a collector fans out over. A collector that needs more than this is asking the wrong tier.

rule.description: The selection rule in force. `league-allowlist` is the placeholder in use until broadcast availability can answer which matches are actually watchable in the US, at which point `us-watchable` replaces it without the collector interface changing.

leagues.description: League ids the allowlist admitted. Present for `league-allowlist`.
